scope: Primary Microsoft sources for a visual and interaction proposal, not a runtime conformance certification.

sources.title: Design principles - Fluent 2 Design System
supportedClaims: Fluent prioritizes familiarity with each platform, an experience that supports focus, and inclusive design.
Reduced visual noise supports calm and confident use.
Native patterns and components should carry most of the experience.
sources.interpretation: The security context strip and the exact navigation grouping are product-specific design decisions.

sources.title: Color - Fluent 2 Design System
supportedClaims: Neutral surfaces establish visual hierarchy.
Brand colors should be applied sparingly because large or repeated areas can weaken hierarchy.
Semantic colors communicate status and should not be used as decoration.
Meaning should not depend on color alone.
Semantic design tokens make color usage consistent.
Windows interaction-state color behavior differs from the web pattern.
sources.interpretation: The exact light/dark hexadecimal values in the rationale are proposed project tokens, not copied platform resource values.

sources.title: Typography - Fluent 2 Design System
supportedClaims: Fluent's Windows type ramp uses Segoe UI Variable.
The documented Windows ramp includes caption 12/16, body 14/20, subtitle 20/28, and title 28/36.
Clear type hierarchy helps users scan and navigate content.
Standard text should have at least 4.5:1 contrast; qualifying large text should have at least 3:1.
Sentence case and consistent text alignment improve readability.
sources.interpretation: Monospace utility text is a product choice for identifiers and generated strings. Contrast still requires artifact and implementation verification.

sources.title: Mica material - Windows apps
supportedClaims: Mica is an opaque, theme-aware application foundation material.
Microsoft recommends placing it behind other content, with visibility in the title bar.
Content can follow standard contiguous or segmented card layering patterns.
Mica has solid-color fallbacks for inactive windows, transparency preferences, and other system conditions.
High-contrast preferences replace Mica with the user's chosen background.
sources.interpretation: A static diagram only approximates material appearance and does not reproduce the user's wallpaper-dependent backdrop.

sources.title: Dialog controls - Windows apps
supportedClaims: Dialogs are modal and should communicate a clear objective or material confirmation.
A safe dismissal action is required; ContentDialog provides this through CloseButton.
Execution actions appear to the left and the safe action appears to the right.
Use concise action-specific button labels.
Field-specific validation should appear inline instead of in a dialog.
Only one ContentDialog can be open in a window at a time.
A default dialog button can respond automatically to Enter.
sources.interpretation: Avoiding a destructive default and calibrating confirmation severity are product safety decisions based on the documented control behavior.

sources.title: Keyboard interactions - Windows apps
supportedClaims: Windows apps should support complete and predictable keyboard interaction.
Actionable controls need logical tab stops and appropriate initial focus.
Visible focus indicates where an action can be performed.
Arrow-key navigation supports familiar list and grouped-control patterns.
Native WinUI controls supply keyboard behavior that custom controls must preserve.
Accelerators and access keys can improve efficiency.
sources.interpretation: Specific accelerator assignments in the rationale are proposed and require conflict and behavior review.

sources.title: Accessibility overview - Windows apps
supportedClaims: Accessible Windows apps support keyboard and assistive technology use as well as user customization.
XAML controls provide built-in accessibility behavior through UI Automation.
Controls require useful accessible names and appropriate roles.
Text size, contrast, display scaling, and high-contrast themes are core accessibility concerns.
Hard-coded styling must not defeat theme and high-contrast resource behavior.
Accessibility requires ongoing implementation verification, including assistive-technology checks.
sources.interpretation: Secret-free accessible names and restrained TOTP announcements are password-manager design requirements derived from the product's sensitive content.

sourceCaveat: Microsoft Learn responses contained generic sign-in text in page chrome, but the referenced article bodies were publicly retrievable. All claims above paraphrase those article bodies.
